_readme: The improv stage, its story scene cards and the director's notes.

set: one bare improv stage for every story. 'places' and 'props' are the only targets and items an action may name; the game turns any other name into 'looks around'. The places stand in for whatever a story needs, and each card's premise says what the Riser plays. The 'what' text of a place is public, like the rest of the set and the card. Keep the names short: the input LLM and the robots' actions (T19) use them.

cards: each one is a comedy version of a famous story. A card's 'seats' are dealt in random order to the actors on stage at Scene Prep, so scene 2 of a 4-actor show uses 3 of its 4 seats. Every want must work when any one seat is left out. 'backdrop' is the scene's painted backdrop flat (T17): an id and one line that describes it. The game sends actors only the card's title and premise, plus each seat's role and want.

Story rules: public-domain stories (Shakespeare, fairy tales, classic novels) can stay close to the original. Modern films and books are parodied only: new names, no trademarked terms or made-up words from them, no quotes, no logos. No real people's names. Tools/check_prompts.py lists the words from each modern original that must never show up, in the files or in a reply.

notes: each scene draws one note. Every actor gets 'note', except one random actor, who gets 'decoy'. A note applies during the scene's 3 turns. Notes are mostly physical, so the log shows who follows them, and each one must work in every story. Notes never ask everyone to grab the same single prop.

places.name: Center
places.what: the middle of the stage, under the main spotlight

places.name: Front
places.what: the front edge of the stage, by the footlights and the audience

places.name: Back
places.what: the back of the stage, in front of the painted backdrop

places.name: Riser
places.what: a sturdy wooden box that plays whatever the story needs: a balcony, a throne, a cockpit, a lookout tower

places.name: Prop Table
places.what: the table at the side of the stage that holds the props

cards.title: Wherefore Art Thou, Robot?
cards.premise: Verona, at night. The Montagues and the Capulets are feuding again. After the Capulet party, a Montague has sneaked into the garden below Juliet's balcony. The Riser is the balcony.

backdrop.what: A moonlit Verona garden: an ivy-covered wall, a stone balcony and a big paper moon.

seats.want: Declare your love from below the balcony, with a gift, before any Capulet catches you.
Hold court from the balcony, and make anyone who loves you prove it with a gift.
Keep the lovers' secret, while telling everyone every other secret you know.
Find the Montague who sneaked in, and challenge him to a duel with the cardboard sword.

cards.title: The Sword in the Stone, Some Assembly Required
cards.premise: Old Britain. A sword is stuck in a stone on the Riser, and whoever pulls it out becomes king. Half the kingdom has queued up to try. The sword is the cardboard sword.

backdrop.what: A castle courtyard with striped banners, a crowd of painted knights and a big gray stone.

seats.want: Find a sword for your knight before the tournament starts. Any sword will do.
Make sure the right person pulls out the sword, then take all the credit.
Wear the paper crown, with or without the sword.
Hand a sword to the most worthy actor on stage, then change your mind about who that is.

cards.title: The Case of the Stolen Rubber Chicken
cards.premise: A foggy night at a London manor. The Duchess's priceless rubber chicken has been stolen, and the great detective Sherlock Ohms has locked every suspect in the study. The Riser is the Duchess's armchair.

backdrop.what: A Victorian study at night: tall bookshelves, a crackling fireplace and a window full of London fog.

seats.want: Name the thief, with one clue from every actor on stage.
Agree with every deduction, and read the clues aloud from the scroll.
Get your rubber chicken back from the armchair, and blame the butler, whoever that is.
Hide the rubber chicken somewhere nobody will look, and stay above suspicion.

cards.title: My Father, the Heavy Breather
cards.premise: Planet Dust, a desert world with two suns. A farm kid dreams of the stars and fixes a battered space truck. Then a masked villain in a black cape lands, breathing very loudly, with family news. The Riser is the space truck's cockpit.

backdrop.what: A desert at dusk under two suns, with a rusty dome hut and a battered space truck.

seats.want: Leave this dusty planet in the space truck on the Riser, today.
Wear the cape, breathe loudly, and reveal a shocking family secret to someone on stage.
Teach anyone who will listen your ancient art of waving the cardboard sword.
Get paid up front before you fly anyone off this planet.

cards.title: The Unsinkable, Probably
cards.premise: 1912, the first voyage of the S.S. Unsinkable, the biggest ship ever built. An iceberg is dead ahead, and nobody on the bow is paying attention. The Riser is the ship's bow, and the lifeboats are at the Back.

backdrop.what: The deck of a grand ocean liner at night, with four smokestacks, a sky full of stars and an iceberg on the horizon.

seats.want: Get someone rich to stand with you on the bow and admire the view.
Get rid of the paper crown, your family's priceless tiara, before your fiancé sees you without it.
Convince everyone the ship is fine. Absolutely fine.
Be first into the lifeboats at the Back, and look heroic doing it.

cards.title: Welcome to Dino Island, Mostly Safe
cards.premise: A billionaire built a theme park of cloned dinosaurs on a tropical island. It is opening day, the fences just lost power, and the tour group is still out in the park. The Riser is the lookout tower.

backdrop.what: A steamy jungle with a broken electric fence, a tilted warning sign and giant footprints in the mud.

seats.want: Convince everyone the park is perfectly safe, and sell each guest a souvenir from the Prop Table.
Get everyone up the lookout tower before something big shows up.

seats.role: A runaway dinosaur with tiny arms
seats.want: Roar at everyone, and grab whatever your tiny arms can reach.
Pet a dinosaur, no matter what the grown-ups say.

notes.decoy: Move to the Back at least once.

notes.note: Move to Center in your first turn, then never move anywhere else.
notes.decoy: Move to the Front in your first turn, then never move anywhere else.

notes.note: Grab a prop in your first turn and hold it all scene. Never throw it or give it away.
Give something to another actor every turn.
notes.decoy: Never give anything to anyone. Keep everything you grab.

notes.note: Throw something at least once, at the actor you trust least.
Climb onto the Riser at least once.
notes.decoy: Never set foot on the Riser.

notes.note: Move to a different place every turn.
notes.decoy: Never move. Stay where you are all scene.

notes.note: Start every turn by looking at another actor.
Mention the rubber chicken every time you speak.
End every line with a question.
